dinkum-3.meaning: All facts kept: the 227-year-old hemlock, 1791, "gusts of reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 km/h)", the whisky barrel, Clinton not related, VP 1805–1812, the magnolia and the sequoia. "with bits set aside for special projects" and "delivered in a whisky barrel, no less" are colour on original points.
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "got knocked flat on Friday by gusts", "Washington's own patch", "as a pressie", "It's not the only old US tree to come a gutser lately" (a heavy fall, apt for a toppled tree). "governments" for administrations is a fair Aussie rendering.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like an Aussie telling the story: "the Mount Vernon mob", "come a gutser", "pressie", "cos the first White House wasn't built yet". "So get this." is a slightly stock opener.
dinkum-3.register: Right at level 3: a steady sprinkle of Aussie through the piece ("own patch", "mob", "pressie", "no less", "come a gutser") without turning it into a pub yarn. No swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the light, curious news-item tone, a touch chattier: "And no, the New York governor's no relation to the 42nd President Bill Clinton".
dinkum-3.flow: Smooth throughout: "The hemlock went in back in 1791, and it got knocked flat on Friday by gusts of reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 km/h)."
dinkum-3.variety: Varied: "taken out", "knocked flat", "patch", "mob", "pressie", "no less", "come a gutser"; nothing repeated.
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the same story of the fallen Mount Vernon hemlock and its history, retold: "It was sent down by New York Governor George Clinton as a pressie, delivered in a whisky barrel, no less."

dinkum-4.meaning: All facts kept: "gathered up to be preserved and put towards special projects", "reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 kph)", the barrel, the Clinton note, the other fallen trees.
dinkum-4.sense: Mostly fits: "own place", "as a pressie", "it rocked up in a whisky barrel". "the people running the Mount Vernon estate reckoned the Canadian hemlock had been gathered up" makes a factual report sound like an opinion.
dinkum-4.authenticity: Natural where used: "cos the first White House wasn't finished yet", "it rocked up in a whisky barrel", "no relation". Nothing forced.
dinkum-4.register: A little light for level 3: a handful of terms ("reckoned", "pressie", "rocked up", "cos") over mostly plain retelling. No swearing.
dinkum-4.tone: Keeps the newsy, mildly curious tone: "It's not the only bit of US history to come down lately, either."
dinkum-4.flow: Reads smoothly: "The hemlock went in the ground in 1791 and came down in Friday's gusts, which were reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 kph)."
dinkum-4.variety: Modest range; "come down" and "came down" do double duty for falling ("came down in Friday's gusts", "to come down lately").
dinkum-4.essence: Clearly the same story with its distinctive whisky-barrel and Clinton details: "it rocked up in a whisky barrel".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All facts kept, including "used for special projects", "gusts reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 kph)", "it turned up in a whisky barrel", and the Clinton and other-trees details.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "took out a 227-year-old tree", "the mob that runs the Mount Vernon estate", "It's not the only bit of US history to go over lately".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural but sparse: "the mob that runs", "cos the first White House wasn't finished yet". Most lines are plain English ("sent it as a present").
yarn-dinkum.register: Light for level 3, closer to level 2: only a few markers ("took out", "mob", "cos", "go over") and "present" where an Aussie retelling would likely say pressie. No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the original news tone intact: "The hemlock, planted back in 1791, came down on Friday in gusts reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 kph)."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth: "According to the Mount Vernon people, the hemlock is the best documented tree on the whole estate: New York Governor George Clinton sent it as a present, and it turned up in a whisky barrel."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Limited slang, and "came down" and "come down" repeat ("came down on Friday", "has come down too").
yarn-dinkum.essence: Clearly the original story, lightly retold: "it turned up in a whisky barrel".
